name: Shared Prompt Plan
description: Keep project prompts shared by content in normal project flows, avoid prompt copy semantics, and make judgment reuse and visibility consistent across queueing, marts, and review details.

userStories.title: Add clone prompt-edit isolation regressions
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want regression coverage for clone prompt edits so that changing a cloned project's prompt cannot mutate or redirect the source project's prompt or judgment behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Add regression coverage that clones a project, edits the cloned project's prompt content, reruns clone judgments, and verifies the source project still points at its original prompt row.
The regression proves the edited clone repoints to a different immutable prompt row while the source project keeps its original prompt id, prompt content, and prompt-linked behavior.
Run the new targeted regression suite before behavior changes and keep the baseline result as pre-change evidence when a newly added regression exposes an existing bug.

userStories.title: Add cloned-project config rerun regression matrix
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want clone rerun regressions for every judgment-affecting project setting so that changing the clone's config cannot accidentally reuse or overwrite source-project judgments.
acceptanceCriteria: Add regression coverage for cloned-project reruns after changing `model_id`, `use_title`, `use_abstract`, `use_fulltext`, and `use_fulltext_no_images`.
Each changed-setting scenario proves the clone does not reuse source judgments and the source project's stored prompt links and judgment visibility remain unchanged.
Add a positive unchanged-clone regression proving rerunning judgments still reuses shared judgments only when prompt id, model id, and content flags all match exactly.

userStories.title: Canonicalize immutable prompt lookup by content hash
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want immutable prompt lookup to be keyed by prompt content rather than archived state so that shared prompts keep one canonical row per hash in normal project flows.
acceptanceCriteria: Update immutable prompt lookup so `app.prompt.archived` does not create parallel prompt identities for the same content hash.
Define the canonical behavior for relinking a hash-matching prompt row whose global `app.prompt.archived` flag is already `TRUE` and keep one-row-per-hash semantics in normal project flows.
Project create, edit, and clone flows continue to work safely with historical mixed prompt rows, including legacy rows with `NULL` content hashes.

userStories.title: Audit remaining origin project semantics
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the remaining `origin_project_id` paths narrowed to true legacy needs so that clone and edit flows no longer depend on project-owned prompt assumptions.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit model-detach and archived-project cleanup paths against shared prompt links instead of project-owned prompt copies.
Keep normal create, edit, clone, and import flows writing `NULL` for `origin_project_id`.
Remove or quarantine any remaining active ownership semantics that are not required by detach recovery or archived-project cleanup.

userStories.title: Create shared project-visible judgment rule
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want one reusable project-visible judgment rule so that fallback reads and mart rebuilds use the same scope, prompt, model, and content-flag eligibility logic.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a shared server-side rule or helper that determines whether a target project may see or reuse a judgment based on project scope, enabled prompt links, model id, and content flags.
The shared rule keeps project or import-route membership out of the intrinsic judgment natural key while preventing out-of-scope visibility or skipped work.
The shared rule is reusable from both raw fallback readers and mart rebuild flows instead of duplicating diverging SQL conditions.

userStories.title: Apply shared visibility rule to review-details fallback
userStories.description: As a user, I want stale or running review details to show the same reusable judgments as fresh mart-backed views so that fallback reads do not hide valid shared judgments.
acceptanceCriteria: When review-detail mart data is stale or running, the raw `app.judgment` fallback returns judgments visible to the target project under the shared rule instead of using same-project-only filtering.
Keep any cross-project diagnostic or `allJudgments` surface separate from the main project-visible judgments list.
Add or update review-details tests for reused visible judgments and out-of-scope exclusions.

userStories.title: Lock queue reuse and scope safeguards
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want queue reuse logic to stay strict about judgment-affecting inputs so that reruns only skip work when the clone truly matches an existing judgment.
acceptanceCriteria: Queue reuse remains keyed by `article_id`, `prompt_id`, `model_id`, `use_title`, `use_abstract`, `use_fulltext`, and `use_fulltext_no_images` with explicit regression coverage for changed clone settings.
Queue filtering only skips work for articles actually in the target project's scope and does not leak out-of-scope reused judgments.
Add or update queue tests so unchanged clone settings reuse safely and changed clone settings do not reuse.

userStories.title: Align large rebuild shared-judgment behavior
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want large rebuild mart logic to match incremental refresh shared-judgment behavior so that rebuilt review surfaces do not disagree with fresh incremental marts.
acceptanceCriteria: Large rebuild shared-judgment eligibility matches incremental mart refresh for matching prompt ids, model ids, and content flags on in-scope articles.
Add or update mart tests proving large rebuild and incremental refresh agree on unchanged clone reuse and changed clone non-reuse.
If any intentional difference remains, document it explicitly and keep review-surface behavior consistent with that decision.
